title: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks For Time-Series Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2606.04074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Adaptive patching has been proposed for time-series forecasting: allocate finer patches where the sequence looks locally informative. We compare three adaptive patching methods with tuned uniform counterparts that use one fixed patch size throughout the input, while preserving each method's backbone family and shared training protocol. Across the evaluated long-horizon benchmarks, we observe mostly small accuracy differences and no consistent advantage for adaptive patching; uniform variants generally train faster and avoid adaptive routing at inference. Motivated by these observations, we develop a theoretical framework for budgeted patch allocation through a common resolution-density representation of uniform, nonuniform, and overlapping layouts, independently of the patching rule. Within a separable shared-loss model, we derive an exact criterion for when nonuniform allocation improves on uniform allocation at the same budge

translated_title: 自适应分块在时间序列预测中比看起来更难
translated_abstract: 自适应分块已被提出用于时间序列预测：在序列看起来局部信息丰富的地方分配更细的分块。我们将三种自适应分块方法与经过调优的均匀分块对应方法进行比较，后者在整个输入中使用一个固定的分块大小，同时保持每种方法的骨干网络家族和共享的训练协议。在所评估的长时程基准测试中，我们观察到精度差异大多很小，自适应分块没有一致的优势；均匀变体通常训练更快，并且在推理时避免了自适应路由。受这些观察的启发，我们通过对均匀、非均匀和重叠布局的统一分辨率-密度表示，开发了一个与分块规则无关的预算化分块分配理论框架。在可分离的共享损失模型中，我们推导出了非均匀分配在相同预算下何时优于均匀分配的精确判据。
tldr: 该论文通过对比实验发现自适应分块相比调优后的均匀分块在长时程预测中并无一致的精度优势，并据此建立了与分块规则无关的预算化分块分配理论框架，推导出相同预算下非均匀分配何时优于均匀分配的精确判据。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that adaptive patching offers no consistent accuracy advantage over tuned uniform patching in long-horizon time-series forecasting, and develops a patch-rule-independent theoretical framework that derives an exact criterion for when nonuniform patch allocation improves on uniform allocation under the same budget.
